name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Hormuz traffic severely depressed after six months of war; US blockade continues and Iran sets conditions for reopening
state: Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 116 Hormuz transits by ships not linked to Iran in the week to 25 Oct, against 124 the week before, and UKMTO had logged 144 incidents since the conflict began (5 Nov brief). Shipping analysts describe traffic as severely depressed after six months of war (Hellenic Shipping News). The US blockade continued on 10 Nov (StratNews Global), and Iran has said the strait reopens only once its conditions are met (Express Tribune, 3 Nov).
for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice and UKMTO guidance for the Gulf region. Disruption affects fuel, gas and freight costs worldwide.

sources.title: Lloyd's List Intelligence — Strait of Hormuz Brief: 5 November 2026
Hellenic Shipping News — Six months of US-Iran war leaves Hormuz traffic severely depressed
StratNews Global — Trump says no new military strikes on Iran, Hormuz blockade continues

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
